decisions.decision: Use synchronous model serving for pre-authorization fraud scores
decisions.context: Each transaction needs a score before authorization, with a response time in the tens of milliseconds. A synchronous request lets the authorization flow use the score directly.
decisions.rationale: It returns a usable score in the authorization path and best fits the stated latency requirement. The service must be provisioned and monitored to keep that dependency responsive.
consequences: Scoring latency needs a defined budget

decisions.decision: Serve low-latency features from an online feature store
decisions.context: The model needs transaction features at scoring time, and feature computation or remote lookups can consume the latency budget. An online store can supply precomputed features quickly.

alternatives.label: Compute features in the scoring service
Fetch features from source systems per request

decisions.rationale: Precomputed features help meet the tight response-time requirement while keeping model inputs reusable. The online store must be kept sufficiently fresh and available.

decisions.context: The service must keep working during traffic peaks. Stateless instances can be scaled horizontally and replaced without coordinating local transaction state.
decisions.rationale: Replicas provide capacity for peaks and reduce the impact of an individual instance failure. This choice depends on shared feature and model dependencies also having suitable availability.

decisions.decision: Record model version and feature snapshot with each score
decisions.context: Auditors must later be able to identify which model version and features produced a score. Recording them alongside the result makes that provenance retrievable after model or feature changes.

alternatives.label: Persist score with model version and feature snapshot
Persist score and model version only

chosen.label: Persist score with model version and feature snapshot

decisions.rationale: The brief requires auditors to know both the model version and features used, so both must be captured with the score. Access controls and retention rules are needed for the stored feature data.
consequences: Each decision creates an audit record
Feature data needs access and retention controls
